fx.fx_commentary: The Canadian dollar firmed to 0.7305 CAD/USD (USD/CAD 1.3688), up 1.5% over the two-week period — the loonie strengthened from approximately 0.72 at the end of March as broader US dollar depreciation sent the DXY toward 98, the lowest level for the dollar index since March 202527. The advance developed against a 125–150 basis point rate differential between the Federal Reserve at 3.50–3.75% and the Bank of Canada at 2.25%, a gap persisting since the BoC's seventh consecutive hold on March 18131. The BoC Summary of Deliberations published April 1 noted near-term growth weaker than the January projection; the next decision on April 29 will include the Monetary Policy Report12. The euro gained 1.34% to 1.1696 EUR/USD, up 6.79% year-over-year, as the ECB held at 2.15% and markets priced a possible June hike on energy-driven inflation3435. Sterling advanced 1.5% to 1.3432 GBP/USD, up 4.7% year-over-year, reflecting the Bank of England base rate at 3.75%36. If the CAD holds near current levels amid the rate differential, the database's 600 transport and logistics projects and 49 manufacturing projects valued at over $67 billion with cross-border trade exposure would carry more favourable USD translation on imported inputs6.

yieldCurve.yield_commentary: The Government of Canada yield curve maintained its normal upward-sloping shape with the 2-year to 10-year spread widening to 67 basis points, up from 63 basis points in the prior edition — the widening developed as the 2-year yield fell 15 basis points to 2.80% while the 10-year declined 11 basis points to 3.47%, reflecting a flight-to-quality bid during the Strait of Hormuz crisis and subsequent position unwinding2829. The 2-year sits 55 basis points above the BoC policy rate of 2.25%, held for a seventh consecutive meeting on March 18, with market pricing at 96.5% probability of a hold on April 29113. Year-over-year, the 2-year has risen 23 basis points from 2.57%, the 10-year has risen 41 basis points from 3.06%, and the 30-year has risen 64 basis points from 3.30% — the 30-year's year-over-year move is the steepest across the six tenors in the Bank of Canada data2829. The 5-year to 10-year spread sits at 29 basis points and the 10-year to 30-year spread at 47 basis points29. If yields hold near current levels amid the continued BoC hold, the 785 power and energy projects and 1,671 infrastructure projects valued at $179 billion in the database would face financing costs anchored at the long end of the curve, while the 211 residential projects valued at $44 billion would retain exposure to the two-year benchmark2829.
